0.long_answer: Aldred Scott Warthin was the first physician to identify the hereditary form of colorectal cancer, now known as Lynch syndrome. In the early 20th century, Warthin conducted detailed studies on a family with a significant history of cancer, publishing his findings in 1913. His work provided some of the earliest evidence that cancer could be inherited. Although later research by Henry T. Lynch significantly advanced the understanding and classification of this condition—so much so that the syndrome bears his name—Lynch himself acknowledged Warthin's pioneering contribution in identifying the hereditary basis of the disease.
